newsitem.title: UK: Vendome hit by poor Far East tourist spend.
newsitem.headline: Vendome hit by poor Far East tourist spend.

text.p: Swiss luxury goods company Vendome Luxury Group reported a 4.6 percent fall in first half profits on Wednesday to 113 million pounds ($188.6 million), hit by lower tourist spending in the Far East.

"The decrease in tourist spending in the Far East, we believe, is a direct result of the weakening of the yen in the second half of last year, and the combination of these two factors has particularly affected those of our brands which have a greater proportion of their sales in the Far East," said chairman Joseph Kanoui.
In Swiss franc terms, pretax profits fell 2.1 percent to 214.7 million in the six months to September 30.
"The reduction in tourist spending in the Far East is, we believe, a short-term phenomenon which will reverse when the yen recovers its strength," added Kanoui.

In pounds sterling, turnover grew 0.6 percent to 703.6 million pounds. Sales of jewellery in the first half decreased below last year by 17.4 percent and sales of leather goods, most dependent on consumer demand in the Far East, fell by 2.3 percent.

Sales of watches rose by 10.4 percent and writing instrument sales increased by 1.7 percent over last year. Perfume sales showed an increase of 20.4 percent over last year reflecting the success of the new Cartier fragrance launched in the second half of last year, but menswear sales were slightly down.

Cartier, founded in 1847 in Paris now has 164 retail outlets and provides an estimated 80 percent of group profits. Other Vendome brands include luxury writing goods maker Mont Blanc and Alfred Dunhill.
Analysts forecasts for pretax profits ranged from 125 to 135 million pounds. Vendome shares were indicated 16p lower at 524-1/2 in early London trade. ($1=.5990 Pound)
